title: Flow Control Nodes 🔀
description: Master Branch, Sequence, Loops, and Gates to control logic flow.

slides.title: Making Decisions 🤔
slides.content:
# The Branch Node

A **Branch** node acts like an **if‑else** statement in code. It checks a Boolean condition and splits execution:

* **True** output → runs if condition is true
* **False** output → runs if condition is false

Example: If `PlayerHealth > 0`, heal; else, die.

Right‑click → **Branch** to add it. Connect a Boolean to the **Condition** input.

quizData.question: A Branch node can have more than two output execution paths.
quizData.explanation: Branch has exactly two outputs: True and False. For multiple conditions, chain branches or use a Switch node.

slides.title: Sequences – Do Many Things 📋
slides.content:
## One Event, Multiple Actions

A **Sequence** node fires several outputs **in order** (top to bottom).

* Each output is a separate execution line.
* All outputs run sequentially (not simultaneously).
* Use when you need to do A, then B, then C from one event.

Example: On BeginPlay → Sequence → [ Print Hello, Set PlayerHealth, Play Sound ].

Add more outputs via the **Add pin +** button on the node.

slides.title: Loops – Doing Things Repeatedly 🔁
slides.content:
## Repeat Until Done

Unreal provides several loop nodes:

* **For Loop** – runs a set number of times (first index to last index). Use the **Index** output to know the current iteration.
* **For Each Loop** – iterates over an array, one element at a time.
* **While Loop** – repeats as long as a condition is true (be careful: it can freeze the game if you never set condition to false!)

Loops are **blocking** – they finish before execution continues past the loop. For background work, use Timers.

quizData.question: Which loop would you use to iterate over every element in an array?
quizData.explanation: For Each Loop automatically runs for each element in an array, giving you the current element.

slides.title: Do N, Delay & Gate 🚦
slides.content:
## More Control

* **Do N** – executes the next node only N times, then stops. Useful for limited actions.
* **Delay** – pauses execution for a given time (in seconds). Connect to the **Completed** output for what happens after.
* **Gate** – controls whether execution can pass through. Use **Open**/ **Close** inputs to toggle. Perfect for enabling/disabling features.

Delay is **non‑blocking** – other graphs keep running. Use it instead of a long loop with Tick.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Flip Flop

**Flip Flop** alternates between A and B outputs each time it's called. Great for toggling a light on/off. Right‑click → Flip Flop.
